title: Adaptive Launch Signal Matrix and Runway for Componentized Inference Stack
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Problem: Our current release gating is binary and component-agnostic; it creates late-stage stalls when one component (eg. runtime batching) meets SLOs but another (eg. console rollout) has outstanding docs or release notes. Goal: Create an adaptive launch signal matrix and operational runway that lets us do progressive rollouts across API, Console, and Runtime while ensuring coordinated release notes, GTM comms, and safe rollback triggers. This ticket scopes the playbook, signoff checklist, telemetry thresholds, and ownership model for release gates.

Key deliverables:
- Signal matrix defining primary + secondary telemetry signals for each component (latency P50/P95, error budget burn rate, rollout health, KB/docs readiness).
- Scope-lock rules tied to signals with explicit "soft lock" vs "hard lock" semantics and cut-window definitions.
- Release notes and comms checklist that maps content owners to signals and final cut deadlines.
- Runway timeline template for staggered progressive rollouts and canaries (percent tiers + time windows).
- Quick rollback criteria and automated fallback routing policy for runtime variants.
- Runbook links and checklist for on-call and GTM during launch windows.

Trade-offs considered:
- More granular signals reduce cross-team blocking but increase coordination overhead; balance by limiting to 6 signals per component (2 primary, 4 secondary).
- Conservative defaults (fail-closed on critical security signals, fail-open on non-customer-facing docs) to minimize user risk while avoiding unnecessary full rollbacks.

Stakeholders: PM (Sofia Patel), Eng leads (Liam Chen - Runtime, Priya Natarajan - API), Console PM (Diego Ramos), Design (Maya Ortiz), GTM/Comms (Hannah Lee), Support (Rajiv Menon).
